blindIndex.description: Blind index vectors. The key is a blind index key and is deliberately not the key the envelope vectors use: they are different secrets and mixing them would be a mistake worth making visible here.

vectors.description: a NIK, under the default normalisation
a NIK written with separators, under the NIK rule
vectors.note: Indexes identically to the plain NIK above. That agreement is the whole reason the NIK rule exists.

vectors.description: a NIK with a trailing non-breaking space
vectors.note: U+00A0. Arrives whenever a value is pasted from a word processor or a spreadsheet. panda-php removed ASCII whitespace only and failed this vector until 0.2.1.

vectors.description: a value with non-ASCII letters
vectors.note: panda-php lowercased ASCII only and failed this vector until 0.2.1.

vectors.description: a value padded with ideographic spaces
vectors.note: U+3000. Removed by the Unicode White_Space property, which Go and panda-php implement and Node.js and Python approximate differently.

vectors.description: a value with surrounding spaces, not normalised at all
an email, which is what the lowercase rule is for
a name under the NIK rule — this one indexes the same as every other name
vectors.note: The hazard, pinned deliberately. The NIK rule strips everything that is not a digit, so this normalises to the empty string — and so does every other value without digits. One index, shared by all of them. See blind-index-format.md.

tokenFormat.description: Access token format vectors. These pin the one accepted spelling of a token: panda_(demo|live)_ followed by 48 or 64 lowercase hex characters. They exist because the pattern was written out in four implementations and several documents, and one of the copies accepted 48 characters where the rest accepted 48 or 64.

vectors.description: a demo token with 48 hex characters
a live token with 48 hex characters
a demo token with 64 hex characters
a live token with 64 hex characters
digits only, which are hex
all zeroes, which are hex
uppercase hex, which must be rejected
vectors.note: A token is compared byte-for-byte against what the portal issued. Accepting both spellings would let a token pass the local check and then fail at the portal.

vectors.description: mixed-case hex, which must be rejected
a single uppercase character among 47 lowercase ones
47 hex characters, one short
49 hex characters, one over
63 hex characters, one short of the second allowed length
vectors.note: 48 and 64 are the only two lengths. 63 is not close to 64; it is a different, unsupported format.

vectors.description: 65 hex characters, one over the second allowed length
an uppercase prefix
an uppercase type
a type that is not demo or live
a wrong prefix
a non-hex character in the payload
leading whitespace
trailing whitespace
an embedded newline
a trailing newline, which must be rejected
vectors.note: The one case where the four engines disagreed on an identical pattern. In Python and PCRE, $ also matches before a trailing newline, so these bytes were a valid token in panda-py and panda-php and invalid in panda-node and panda-go. A token read from a file or pasted out of a heredoc carries one routinely, so the same string would have passed a local check in two SDKs and failed the portal.

vectors.description: a trailing carriage return
a trailing CRLF, as a Windows file would carry
a leading newline
an empty string

tokenFormat.patternNote: Written with $ because that is how three of the four engines spell it. Python and PCRE give $ a second meaning — it also matches immediately before a newline at the end of the subject — so those two must use \Z and the D modifier respectively. Without that, the trailing-newline vector below passes in Node and Go and fails in the other two.
